name: Question 1
problem:
Let ${v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]$ and ${v}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -1\end{aligned}]$ be eigenvectors of a matrix $A$ that correspond to eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{1}=4$ and ${\lambda }_{2}=0,$ respectively.
What is the general solution of the matrix differential equation ${x}^{′}(t)=Ax(t)?$

Let v1=[−21] and v2=[3−1] be eigenvectors of a matrix A that correspond to eigenvalues λ1=4 and λ2=0, respectively. What is the general solution of the matrix differential equation x′(t)=Ax(t)?

a
x(t)=c1[3−1]e4t,c1∈R
b
x(t)=c1[−21]e4t+c2[3−1]et,c1,c2∈R
c
x(t)=c1[−21]e4tc1∈R
d
x(t)=c1[−21]e4t+c2[3−1],c1,c2∈R
e
x(t)=c1[−21]+c2[3−1]e4t,c1,c2∈R
